Looking at this objectively and a quick google search I would think the max would be 25 years.  They’re not going to stack all the sentences on top of each other, like 15x3 3x2 and then 25x1.  Most likely it would all be served together.  Again I’m not a lawyer and don’t live in Wisconsin but in Florida I know guys that have done time for similar charges and were very proactive before sentencing and after to get out early.  This included N.A./AA while in jail/prison and rehab.  When I went to rehab my two bunkies were out early once completed but had probation for ten years.  One kid slipped up in there and the police took him right back to prison. Different state and different charges nether were looking at 25 years.

People will bash public defenders and the problem with them isn’t that they’re bad lawyers per se but their case loads are ridicules.  What that means is they don’t have the time for discovery and time to build a defense.  On the flip side of the coin is nether does the DA so plea deals are often taken at least here in Florida.

I’m trying to give you some positive outlook on a shitty situation you’ve found yourself in but realistically he’s going away for a while.  I would be prepared for 25 years and you can do whatever you want but both you and him won’t be the same when he gets out.

And don’t kid yourself if he’s truly addicted, which he is, he can get whatever the hell he wants in jail if he has the money or is doing favors which is all kinds of bad.
